newsitem.title: USA: PanEnergy unit boosting Midwest capacity.
newsitem.headline: PanEnergy unit boosting Midwest capacity.

text.p: PanEnergy Corp's Texas Eastern Transmission Corp said Friday it plans to boost natural gas capacity by 250 million cubic feet per day through its Lebanon Lateral pipeline in Indiana and Ohio in 1998.

The pipeline said the $31 million expansion will provide additional capacity for the company's Spectrum project, which will move up to 500 million cubic feet per day of natural gas from the Chicago area to East Coast markets.
The PanEnergy Corp subsidiary said the upgrade will increase its capacity in the Lebanon Lateral to 650 million cubic feet per day.
The 114-mile lateral was constructed in 1990 to link PanEnergy's four interstate pipelines -- Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line Co, Trunkline Gas Co, Texas Eastern and Algonquin Gas Transmission Co.
The expansion plans call for installing 17,000 additional horsepower at compressor stations at Glen Carn, Ohio, and Gas City, Ind.
Texas Eastern said it will file plans for the Lebanon Lateral expansion project with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission by early June.
